decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule condition C2 fails: with correct task-major ordering, |Spearman(R, canonical)| = 0.23 (p=0.31) and |Spearman(R, weighted)| = 0.21 (p=0.36), both below the 0.30 threshold; eta-squared(R, page_type) = 0.144 < 0.20. C1 passes (CV=0.70 > 0.10). C1 AND NOT C2 triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING per spec.json decision_rule. The producer's claimed C2 pass was an artifact of definition-major data ordering (all DEF-FULL-MAP first, then all DEF-FORM-ONLY, then all ISOLATED-A-LINK), creating artificial monotonic structure. The density ratio is definition-sensitive (10x gap between DEF-FORM-ONLY and others) but does not significantly correlate with task type or recipe sensitivity in this N=21 sample. NC1 null control also fails: real eta-squared=0.144 vs shuffled mean=0.117, task-type structure not statistically significant (permutation p=0.23). C-MEAS-VALID status updated to REJECTED for the density-ratio MIXED metric approach.

claim_updates.reason: Density ratio R = canonical/weighted varies 17x (CV=0.70) but variation is predominantly definition-driven (10x between DEF-FORM-ONLY and DEF-FULL-MAP), not task-type driven (1.78x). The ratio does not significantly correlate with canonical or weighted density after correcting Spearman computation (|rho|≈0.21–0.23, p>0.30), and task-type structure is not statistically significant (eta-squared=0.144 < 0.20 threshold; permutation p=0.23). Frozen decision_rule C2 fails. The density ratio cannot serve as a principled MIXED outcome decision rule for recipe sensitivity in this setting. Claim ceiling bounded to: definition-dependent ratio metric on 7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions, truncated-first-20 sample.

product_action: NONE — density ratio MIXED metric is falsified; product lane must not implement ratio-based MIXED decision rules.
next_question: Given that linear combination recipes and density-ratio metrics both fail to break OECD/COINr degeneracy (mathematical identity and definition-artifact respectively), should the MIXED outcome program pivot to (a) a structurally non-linear third recipe (DOM hierarchy depth, conditional inclusion based on element relationships, semantic role weighting) that could produce rankings outside the canonical-weighted range, or (b) abandon dominance-based MIXED handling entirely and restrict density metric use to recipe-insensitive task-definition pairs only?
reason: The audit identifies CRITICAL computation errors in the producer's Spearman correlations (VF-1): definition-major data ordering created artificial monotonic structure inflating |rho| from 0.21–0.23 to 0.66–0.71. With correct task-major ordering, all three C2 sub-conditions fail (|Spearman|<0.30, eta-squared<0.20). The NC1 null control also fails (VF-2): task-type structure is not statistically significant. The density ratio's 17x range is real but driven by definition choice (DEF-FORM-ONLY captures nearly all elements, making weighted density ~0.98 while canonical stays low), not by task-type-dependent recipe sensitivity. The ratio conflates definition artifacts with task-type effects (VF-3, VF-6). The frozen decision_rule yields FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (C1 AND NOT C2).
